## Station Overview

The **Mind Palace** station tests short-term memory using a classic word list paradigm. Participants study a list of 10 words, complete a distractor task, then recall as many words as possible. This station demonstrates the **serial position effect** — the tendency to remember words at the beginning (primacy) and end (recency) of a list better than those in the middle.

Additionally, this station implements a **between-groups manipulation**: Lab 304A sees abstract words with background music, while Lab 304B sees concrete words in silence.

## What Participants Do

1. **STUDY (30 seconds)**: Memorise 10 words shown on screen
2. **DISTRACT (60 seconds)**: Complete simple maths problems
3. **RECALL (90 seconds)**: Write down as many words as remembered on paper
4. **RECORD**: Enter results in Qualtrics — total recalled, which positions, intrusions

## Research Questions

> Do participants recall more words from the beginning and end of the list (serial position effect)?

> Do concrete words lead to better recall than abstract words (between-labs comparison)?

> Does background music affect memory performance?

## Experimental Design

| Element | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Design | Between-groups (lab room) + Within-subjects (serial position) |
| IV 1 | Word type: Abstract (Lab 304A) vs Concrete (Lab 304B) |
| IV 2 | Serial position (positions 1–10) |
| DV | Number of words correctly recalled |
| Controls | Same presentation time, same distractor task |

## Data Variables

| Variable | Type | Description | Range |
|----------|------|-------------|-------|
| `mem_total` | Count | Words correctly recalled | 0–10 |
| `mem_pos1` – `mem_pos10` | Categorical | Recalled each position? | Yes, No, Unsure |
| `mem_intrusions` | Count | False memories (wrong words) | 0–10 |
| `mem_strategy` | Text | Strategy used (if any) | Open text |

## Between-Groups Conditions

| Lab Room | Word Type | Background |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| 304A | Abstract words | Music playing |
| 304B | Concrete words | Silence |

::: {.callout-note}
## Word Types
- **Concrete words**: Easily visualised (e.g., apple, chair, dog)
- **Abstract words**: Cannot be directly sensed (e.g., justice, freedom, thought)

Research typically shows concrete words are easier to remember due to dual-coding (visual + verbal).
:::

## Serial Position Effect

| Position | Effect | Explanation |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| 1–3 | **Primacy** | More rehearsal time, transferred to long-term memory |
| 4–7 | **Asymptote** | Less rehearsal, interference from adjacent items |
| 8–10 | **Recency** | Still in short-term memory at recall |

## Expected Results

| Metric | Typical Range |
|--------|---------------|
| Total recalled | 5–7 out of 10 |
| Primacy (pos 1–3) | 60–80% recall |
| Middle (pos 4–7) | 40–60% recall |
| Recency (pos 8–10) | 70–90% recall |
| Intrusions | 0–2 words |

## Suggested Analyses

**Primary analyses:**

- [Independent t-test](../analysis/independent-t-test.qmd) comparing Lab 304A vs 304B on total recall
- Serial position curve (line graph of recall % by position)

**Descriptive statistics:**

- [Mean](../statistics/mean.qmd) total recall per lab room
- Proportion recalled at each position

**Exploratory analyses:**

- Do intrusions differ between labs?
- Does strategy use predict performance?

## R Code Starter

```r
# Load data
datalab <- read_csv("datalab_data.csv")

# Compare total recall between labs
datalab |>
  group_by(lab_room) |>
  summarise(
    mean_recall = mean(mem_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_recall = sd(mem_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  )

# Independent t-test
t.test(mem_total ~ lab_room, data = datalab)

# Serial position analysis
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Convert position data to long format
position_data <- datalab |>
  select(participant_id, lab_room, mem_pos1:mem_pos10) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("mem_pos"),
    names_to = "position",
    values_to = "recalled"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    position = parse_number(position),
    recalled = if_else(recalled == "Yes", 1, 0)
  )

# Calculate proportion recalled at each position
serial_curve <- position_data |>
  group_by(position) |>
  summarise(prop_recalled = mean(recalled, na.rm = TRUE))

# Plot serial position curve
ggplot(serial_curve, aes(x = position, y = prop_recalled)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#275882", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(colour = "#EA8439", size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    x = "Serial Position",
    y = "Proportion Recalled",
    title = "Serial Position Curve"
  )
```

## Connection to Other Concepts

This station demonstrates:

- [Between-Groups Design](../design/between-groups-design.qmd) — different participants in different conditions
- [Independent t-test](../analysis/independent-t-test.qmd) — comparing two independent groups
- [Mean](../statistics/mean.qmd) — summarising recall performance

## Tips for Facilitators

- This station is completed **together** as a whole-lab activity
- Ensure participants only look at **their assigned list** (left or right side of screen)
- The 60-second distractor task is crucial — it clears short-term memory
- Remind participants to write on paper during recall, not look back at the screen
- Intrusions (false memories) are valuable data — encourage honest reporting
